newsitem.title: UK: London gold extends losses, fixes at new low.
newsitem.headline: London gold extends losses, fixes at new low.

text.p: Gold fixed at $357.65 per ounce on Tuesday morning, a fresh 3-1/4 year low, as the market's New Year losses deepened.
The fixing was the lowest since October 6, 1993, when gold fixed at $353.50. On Monday afternoon, the fixing came in at $358.50.
Gold has fallen more than $10 an ounce in the first week of 1997 after coming under heavy selling pressure from speculators and U.S.-based investment funds.
However, the market is heavily oversold and technical analysts said gold was due for a corrective bounce of some $3-$5 before resuming its downward movement.
Prices are eventually likely to tumble to $350 an ounce, or even lower, dealers and analysts said.
The other precious metals, which have been following gold lower, may also see a brief correction higher in the near term but remain vulnerable to further losses, they added.
